entries.title: Ezekiel 38:1
segments: This and the following chapter contain a prophecy of the invasion of "the mountains of Israel" by an immense multitude "out of the north parts," assisted by many allies.  It shall take place "in the latter years," after Israel has been "brought back from the sword, and is gathered out of many people," and is dwelling safely in "unwalled villages;" and the invaders shall be overthrown with immense slaughter. It is generally agreed that the fulfilment of this prophecy is yet future.  Perhaps it is the same assault as that predicted in

, which takes place after the binding of Satan for a thousand years. 
 
So far as the powers of darkness are left at liberty, they will stir up wicked men to persecute God's people.  Hereafter, as in past ages, we may expect mighty combinations of ungodly rulers and corrupt teachers to hinder, and if possible extinguish the light and liberty of the gospel.  But God will turn their counsels into foolishness, and make their mischievous plots the means of their own destruction.

entries.title: Ezekiel 38:2
segments: Gog, the land of Magog; Gog seems to be here the leader, and Magog the people.  Magog was descended from Japheth, and is named with other northern tribes,

entries.title: Ezekiel 38:4
segments: Hooks into thy jaws; see note on

. 
 
  Bring thee forth; out of my land.

entries.title: Ezekiel 38:5
segments:
vv 5-6. 
 
  Persia--Togarmah; these are the allies of Gog.

entries.title: Ezekiel 38:7
segments: Be thou prepared; God is here represented as calling forth Gog, that he may meet his final overthrow,

entries.title: Ezekiel 38:8
segments:
Visited; punished; for his invasion of Israel is the occasion of his overthrow.  But many render, "shall be made chief," that is, of all the invading hosts. 
 
  Land that is brought back; land whose people are brought back. 
 
  Always waste; during the long exile of God's people from them. 
 
  It is brought forth; the same as, "the land that is brought back," that is, the people belonging to it are brought forth.

entries.title: Ezekiel 38:11
segments: Land of unwalled villages; these words indicate a long period of peace and security, in which walls have been omitted as unnecessary.

entries.title: Ezekiel 38:13
segments:
Sheba--Dedan--Tarshish; these seem to be the allies of Gog. 
 
  Young lions; princes.

entries.title: Ezekiel 38:17
segments: Of whom I have spoken in old time; compare
.  All these prophets represent the final deliverance of God's people as preceded by a general assault of all their enemies upon them.

entries.title: Ezekiel 38:19
segments:
vv 19-22. 
 
  A great shaking--hailstones, fire, and brimstone; compare
.  Such descriptions are generally to be understood figuratively of the effects of God's wrath.
